incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA); Investment Commission, MOEA (MOEAIC) for foreign investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (with minutes of shareholder subscription), submitted electronically via the MOEA One-Stop Business Startup Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital for a foreign-invested limited company; all shares must be fully subscribed and monetary contributions verified by an accredited CPA via a bank capital remittance account (no escrow requirement).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of Taiwan WFOE Limited with its registered office at [address] is confirmed; that the shares subscribed by the founding member, [Investor], in the amount of NT$[capital] be issued and allocated; that the registered Articles of Incorporation be adopted and filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; that [Name A] be appointed as President/Director, [Name B] as Supervisor, and [Name C] as Corporate Secretary/Finance Manager; that the Management Committee is authorized to open bank accounts, execute documents, engage an agency, and undertake all filings required to complete the foreign investment approval and tax registrations; and that all actions taken by the incorporators prior to this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Company Registration Information System (One-Stop Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log-in to the MOEA startup portal and submit an online name pre-clearance for English and Chinese trade names; ensure no existing identical trade name in the same registered industry; receive an official name approval letter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name conflicts, submit up to three alternative name proposals within 15 days; resubmission is free.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online investment application via MOEAIC 'Investor' system with a construction/secondhand machinery trading business plan, source-of-funds statement, and legalized investor documents; obtain written investment approval before capital remittance.
required_dossiers: Business plan for used excavator wholesale
Investor's Certificate of Incorporation or passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a supplemental document request within 30 days; if denied, appeal to the MOEA administrative review board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated foreign-exchange settlement bank; accredited CPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary NT$ capital remittance account at a licensed bank, wire the approved investment amount from the foreign investor, and instruct a certified CPA to issue a capital contribution verification report after funds are credited.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If remittance is short of approved amount, file a supplemental remittance within 60 days after bank notice; re-verification by CPA required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File incorporation with prescribed Articles of Incorporation (including name, object, capital, shares, governance clauses), registration application, and capital verification; pay official fees and receive the Company Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: Subscription minutes and first board resolution
Registered office lease contract or consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a correction notice, correct and resubmit within 90 days; otherwise the application is voided.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for tax registration (Uniform Invoice Certificate), differential VAT registration, and use of a company seal; register the physical office address and obtain a business license certificate.
required_dossiers: Unified number card and seal card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed or queried, file a written explanation within 15 days and obtain a temporary business start certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and AML Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the operational corporate bank account, complete AML/KYC onboarding, designate signatories for wire transfers and SWIFT letters of credit, and register ultimate beneficial ownership information.
required_dossiers: First board resolution on bank account authority
Company seal and responsible person ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If extra KYC scrutiny is imposed, submit updated shareholder structure and bank statements within 10 days; account may be restricted until clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (advisory; not required for pure trading)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required for wholesale remarketing of used construction equipment; only import/export registration with the Taiwan Directorate General of Customs

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - trading and storage of secondhand machinery without disassembly does not require an EIA report or environmental registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; if temporary storage occurs, waste handling must comply with Waste Management Act; no wastewater or VOC discharge from operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office or showroom premises must pass quarterly fire safety inspection by the local fire department under Public Places Fire Safety Regulations; warehouse structure must hold a building-use permit and load-bearing inspection certificate if equipment is physically stored.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局 / STA); national internet portal: www.chinatax.gov.cn; electronic tax bureau: etax.chinatax.gov.cn; nationwide VAT invoice verification: inv-veri.chinatax.gov.cn; the WFOE's direct day-to-day counterparty is the in-charge competent tax authority (主管税务机关) of its registered address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Following incorporation registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), a WFOE automatically receives its Unified Social Credit Code (统一社会信用代码 / USCC), which is the statutory TIN for all tax, customs, and foreign-exchange filings. Under the multi-license-integration reform, initial tax registration is synchronized with SAMR incorporation data; the WFOE must nevertheless complete post-registration formalities at the in-charge tax authority within 30 days of the business license date, including filing the shareholder register, legal representative and paid-in capital details, financial accounting system filing, bank account reporting, application for the electronic tax registration certificate, and enrolment for e-invoice issuance. Where the WFOE intends to claim export tax refunds (ETR), it must complete export-rebate filing with the tax authority and obtain the Customs declaration registration for import/export enterprises (海关进出口货物收发货人备案).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a CN WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise (居民企业) and a separate unlimited corporate taxpayer; CIT is levied on worldwide income at 25%, and VAT and surcharges are entity-level taxes. The entity is not pass-through eligible; the used-machinery trading scope is in the standard domestic and export taxable territory, and full tax-exempt zone status does not attach unless the WFOE is registered within a comprehensive bonded zone (综合保税区) or the Hainan Free Trade Port, where targeted VAT deferral/zero-rating and income-tax preferential scheduling may apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China has no check-the-box pass-through or hybrid-mismatch election. Available statutory elections include: (i) VAT general taxpayer versus small-scale taxpayer election for taxpayers with annual taxable turnover at or below RMB 5 million, with mandatory general-taxpayer registration above that threshold; (ii) export tax-refund method election between exemption-and-refund (免退税) and exemption-credit-refund (免抵退) where applicable; (iii) secondhand-goods simplified levy election for used-machinery sales (3% levy reduced to 2%) when input VAT cannot be evidenced; and (iv) accounting-basis elections for depreciation methods, inventory valuation, and loss carryforward within the CIT law. Cross-border payments and surplus-stripping arrangements are instead policed through the SAIC transfer-pricing and special tax-adjustment framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no absolute turnover exemption from tax registration: every enterprise, including a WFOE, must complete tax and VAT registration at incorporation. The economically significant threshold is RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales for small-scale taxpayer classification: at or below RMB 5 million the taxpayer may retain simplified small-scale VAT treatment and, within applicable relief policy expiring 31 December 2027, may enjoy exemption from VAT for monthly sales at or below RMB 100,000; once annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5 million, general-taxpayer registration is compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the national fully digitalized electronic invoice platform (全面数字化的电子发票 / 数电票): VAT invoices must be issued and uploaded in real time through the electronic tax bureau, with each invoice bearing a unique digital stamp and verification code. Wholesale used-machinery taxpayers must activate the e-invoice entitlement and adopt digital invoice API/ERP clearance without paper fiscal stamps; the VAT Invoice Management System performs real-time state inspection and risk control on invoice issuance, and erroneous invoices must be cancelled electronically through the platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAT Implementing Rules and current export-tax-rebate (ETR) regulations, exported goods are zero-rated: output VAT on the export sale is 0% and the input VAT attributable to the exported used excavators is refundable by the in-charge tax authority. To claim the zero rate and refund, the WFOE must (1) be a VAT general taxpayer or an entitled small-scale taxpayer under the exemption-and-refund method; (2) sell to a non-PRC purchaser, deliver the machinery out of the PRC customs territory, and declare the export under the used-earthmoving-equipment customs code (HS 8429); (3) evidence a compliant purchase chain through VAT special input invoices or a lawful deemed-input calculation; (4) collect foreign currency from a lawful settlement channel and verify the inward remittance; and (5) file the ETR declaration online before the statutory filing deadline. Used, secondhand, or refurbished machinery remains nominally eligible for zero-rating, but the refund is limited to the actual deductible input VAT evidenced; machinery acquired without valid input invoices may be exported tax-exempt without refund or under the special 2% simplified levy.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) in the name of the WFOE as exporter of record, containing HS 8429 classification and destination TW (Taiwan)
Carrier-issued Bill of Lading / multimodal transport document evidencing physical export of the used excavators
Bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate and Foreign Exchange Collection Confirmation (涉外收入申报单及出口收汇电子数据) proving FX repatriation within the statutory window
Export sales contract and commercial invoice with equipment serial numbers, model, engine hours, and CFR/CIF price allocation
PRC VAT special input invoices (增值税专用发票) and payment records for the procured used machines, spare parts, overhaul, and port services
Packing list, secondhand-equipment inspection report, and registration/displacement certificates required by Customs for used heavy machinery
ETR declaration forms (出口退(免)税申报表) and corresponding electronic clearance data submitted through the online tax system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETR administration imposes strict post-export verification through the STA/Customs data-matching system. Any export rebate later found to be unsupported — for example mismatches among the customs declaration, bill of lading, invoice, or bank receipt; inflated invoice amounts or deductions; or no actual export of the used machines — results in clawback of the rebate received plus statutory late-payment interest, an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the illegally obtained refund amount, downgrade of the taxpayer's ETR credit classification to Category IV for at least six months, suspension or cancellation of future rebate approvals, and referral to the GACC anti-smuggling authority. Criminal exposure under PRC Criminal Law Articles 201 and 204 extends to imprisonment of up to life, forfeiture of property, and criminal fines where refund fraud or false export documents are established; officers of the WFOE and the beneficial owner may be penalized personally, and cross-border schemes using Taiwan-linked conduit documentation are proactively screened for round-tripping and over-invoicing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: For a mainland China wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the principal authorities are the People's Bank of China and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, with foreign-exchange transactions processed through authorized domestic banks. The payload identifies Taiwan as the jurisdiction; Taiwan operations would instead be regulated by the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), the Financial Supervisory Commission, and Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs. A mainland China WFOE should not assume that it may freely maintain or operate Taiwan domestic accounts, and the Taiwan-specific cross-Strait investment and banking restrictions require separate confirmation before implementation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The renminbi is generally convertible for current-account transactions, including genuine trade in goods and services, subject to documentation, bank review, customs and tax data matching, and anti-money-laundering controls. Capital-account transactions remain regulated. A WFOE may receive registered foreign-invested capital, shareholder loans within applicable cross-border financing limits, trade finance, and other approved capital-account funds through designated bank accounts, but conversion and use must comply with SAFE and PBOC rules and the enterprise's registered business scope. Dividend and profit remittance is generally permitted after completion of statutory accounting, tax filing, loss-offset and reserve requirements, approval or filing of the relevant corporate resolutions, and submission of audited financial statements, tax payment or withholding evidence, and bank remittance documentation. Principal hurdles include insufficient distributable profits, unreconciled tax or customs records, overdue foreign-exchange reporting, capital-account misuse, related-party transfer-pricing concerns, sanctions or beneficial-owner concerns, and restrictions applicable to cross-Strait transactions. Foreign-currency balances may normally be retained in permitted accounts; settlement into renminbi is not generally subject to a universal mandatory full-conversion rule, but each conversion must have a lawful purpose and supporting records.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mainland China does not generally impose a universal statutory requirement that all export proceeds be surrendered or converted into renminbi at a fixed ratio. Export proceeds may generally be retained in permitted foreign-currency accounts or settled as required for lawful operating purposes. Export receipts must be collected through authorized banks, supported by genuine underlying trade, and reported or reconciled where required by SAFE, customs, tax and bank systems. There is no single universal statutory deadline applicable to every export transaction or a universal mandatory conversion percentage; delayed collection, advance receipts, unusual payment routes, third-party collection, offset arrangements, and long-aged receivables may trigger bank documentation, SAFE reporting, or enhanced review. The enterprise should maintain export contracts, invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading, logistics records, customer payment evidence, receivables aging, and explanations for delayed or third-party settlement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection and operational support, but low as a substitute for a mainland China licensed bank. An offshore electronic-money institution cannot automatically open a mainland China corporate account, conduct unrestricted renminbi collection or settlement, or perform regulated foreign-exchange, deposit-taking, payment-clearing, or trade-finance activities in China. Use is generally limited to licensed corridors, merchant acquiring, payment initiation, or collection structures permitted in the relevant jurisdictions. Funds should not be commingled with corporate operating cash, and the provider must be screened for licensing, safeguarding, sanctions, data-transfer, beneficial-owner, and cross-border payment compliance. Taiwan-based fintech providers require separate analysis under Taiwan financial and cross-Strait rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mainland Chinese banks commonly require the legal representative or authorized representative, beneficial owners, directors or controlling persons, and key account operators to complete identity verification. Remote video verification may be available on a case-by-case basis, but it is not a guaranteed substitute for branch attendance. A bank may require an in-person visit where the WFOE is newly incorporated, foreign-owned, controlled from a high-risk jurisdiction, engaged in used heavy machinery trading, seeking foreign-exchange or trade-finance services, using complex ownership, or unable to demonstrate a genuine mainland operating presence. The enterprise should prepare certified and legalized foreign corporate documents where required, Chinese translations, passports, proof of address, appointment resolutions, articles of association, business licence, tax registration information, actual-office evidence, employee and warehouse evidence, transaction forecasts, supplier and customer information, and the business-purpose explanation for used excavator and roller imports, exports, resale, repairs, and logistics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional inconsistency between a mainland China WFOE entity identifier and Taiwan being stated as the jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a written jurisdiction memorandum identifying the actual place of incorporation, principal place of business, banking location, tax residence, and transaction corridors. Provide the mainland business licence, company registration extract, registered address, actual operating address, ownership chart, and a separate analysis of any Taiwan subsidiary, branch, representative office, supplier, customer, or payment leg. Do not present Taiwan as the WFOE's domestic banking jurisdiction unless the entity has a legally established and permitted Taiwan presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a newly incorporated WFOE with limited operating history and no demonstrated commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit office lease, warehouse or third-party logistics agreement, hiring records, payroll evidence, tax filings, customs registrations, equipment inspection capability, business plan, board-approved treasury policy, projected monthly cash flows, and executed or draft contracts with identifiable suppliers and customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Used construction excavators and rollers generate enhanced concerns regarding valuation, origin, export-control exposure, sanctions, stolen-property risk, and unusual trade pricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain purchase contracts, serial-number and ownership records, title certificates, inspection reports, photographs, maintenance history, customs classification, country-of-origin evidence, export licences where applicable, sanctions screening, end-user and end-use statements, independent valuation, insurance, shipping documents, and a documented approval process for high-value or higher-risk counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments, unrelated remitters, payment netting, split payments, cash-equivalent settlement, or payments through offshore accounts not named in the contract.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Use contractually designated payer and beneficiary accounts. For exceptions, obtain amended contracts, board or management approval, written commercial rationale, related-party disclosure, identity and beneficial-owner verification, bank confirmation, invoice matching, and a complete reconciliation linking the payment to the underlying shipment or service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-invested capital or shareholder-loan funds are inconsistent with the registered capital, financing limit, source of funds, or stated business purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide shareholder resolutions, capital contribution documents, foreign-investment registration or filing records, source-of-funds evidence, audited shareholder financial statements, loan agreement, cross-border financing calculation, SAFE and bank filing records, contribution schedule, and a restricted-use treasury ledger separating capital funds from trade receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or rapid foreign-exchange conversions, frequent transfers between related entities, or currency conversion unsupported by operating needs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a rolling 13-week cash forecast, approved FX policy, invoices, customs records, payroll and tax obligations, hedging rationale, counterparty exposure report, transfer-pricing support, intercompany agreements, board approvals, and reconciliation of each conversion to a documented current-account or permitted capital-account purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-owner opacity, nominee arrangements, politically exposed persons, sanctions exposure, or high-risk country involvement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a complete ownership and control chart to natural persons, passports and proof of address, corporate registry extracts, trust or foundation documents, PEP and sanctions-screening results, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, management certifications, and independent corporate intelligence where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient tax, customs, foreign-exchange, or statistical reporting history, including aged export receivables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide tax clearance or filing records, VAT and customs declarations, export collection ledger, bank statements, receivables aging, customer confirmations, explanations for delayed collection, SAFE or bank reporting evidence, and a corrective-action timetable for any discrepancy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder capital through the WFOE's designated foreign-invested capital account at an authorized mainland bank. The remittance message should identify the exact shareholder, beneficiary WFOE, registered capital or permitted shareholder-loan purpose, currency, contract or resolution reference, and ultimate beneficial owner. The bank should verify the foreign-investment registration or filing, business licence, capital contribution or loan documentation, source of funds, financing-limit compliance, and consistency with the enterprise's registered business scope. Do not route capital through an employee, unrelated affiliate, personal account, offshore payment wallet, or customer collection account. Following receipt, retain foreign currency or settle through the permitted bank process; maintain a transaction-level ledger distinguishing capital, shareholder loans, trade receipts, and intercompany settlements. For Taiwan-linked capital, separately confirm cross-Strait investment approval, remittance, reporting, and prohibited-sector requirements before initiating the transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary supplier payments, use an authorized bank's cross-border remittance rail, normally SWIFT MT103 or its current ISO 20022 equivalent, with the exact beneficiary legal name, account, bank identifier, invoice number, purchase order, customs or shipment reference, goods description, currency, and payment purpose. For higher-value or documentary transactions, use a commercial letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank-approved trade-finance product supported by the sales or purchase contract, pro forma invoice, customs classification, inspection documents, transport documents, insurance, and end-use information. An LC should specify documentary conditions, permitted Incoterms, partial shipment and transshipment rules, sanctions and export-control representations, discrepancy handling, and reimbursement instructions. Banks may require import-payment registration, customs matching, tax evidence, beneficial-owner screening, and proof that the goods are lawful and commercially priced. Payments must not be split to evade review, routed through undisclosed third parties, or described with generic purposes inconsistent with the underlying machinery trade.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts with an authorized mainland bank, supported by documented trade or financial exposure, approved treasury limits, maturity controls, and evidence of the underlying payable or receivable.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available only where the authorized bank offers the product and applicable mainland rules permit the enterprise and transaction; they should be used for genuine renminbi or foreign-currency exposure and not for speculative trading.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps may be available through qualified banks for genuine financing or operating exposures, subject to bank suitability review, documentation, collateral or credit limits, accounting treatment, and applicable foreign-exchange and derivatives regulations.

Plain-vanilla currency options or option-based hedges may be available through qualified banks where permitted, but require enhanced suitability, premium, valuation, risk-disclosure, board approval, and accounting controls.

The treasury policy should prohibit uncovered speculation, establish hedge-accounting and counterparty limits, require independent confirmation and valuation, document hedge designation, monitor collateral and margin, and reconcile every derivative to a forecast or contractually identifiable exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed by May 31 following the end of the calendar or fiscal year; one-month extension may apply where permitted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax surcharge, interest, assessment by the tax authority, and administrative fines may apply; persistent non-compliance may affect tax registration and business status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company information and beneficial ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally completed during the prescribed annual reporting period, commonly November 1 through January 31; changes to reportable directors, managers, and shareholders holding 10% or more must generally be reported within 15 days of the relevant change or registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company Act penalties generally range from approximately NTD 50,000 to NTD 500,000, with repeated fines until correction; serious or continuing non-compliance may lead to administrative dissolution or revocation procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting and approval of financial statements and profit allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records maintained for shareholder and regulatory inspection; no routine annual filing with a separate authority unless specifically required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the end of each financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or properly document the meeting may create director liability, shareholder remedies, and administrative penalties where statutory filing or reporting obligations are also breached.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit and certification is generally required for public companies and for non-public companies meeting prescribed thresholds, commonly including paid-in capital of at least NTD 30 million, annual net operating revenue of at least NTD 100 million, or total assets of at least NTD 100 million, subject to applicable regulations and exemptions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-adopted IFRS generally applies to public-interest and specified companies; eligible private companies may use Taiwan GAAP or applicable SME accounting standards. Tax accounts must comply with Taiwan tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not generally require a separate annual confirmation solely for every share transfer. The company must update its shareholder register upon valid transfers and report prescribed information concerning directors, managers, and shareholders holding 10% or more, together with required annual confirmations and change reports under the Company Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 500-2,000 annually, excluding mail handling, nominee services, and special compliance work.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 for a small private trading company, depending on transaction volume, inventory complexity, foreign ownership, and audit thresholds.
